//: Type checking for a JavaScript project (RM-002 R-07 / P2).
There are no .ts files here and there is not meant to be one. The library is
clean ESM with thorough JSDoc; this makes that JSDoc mean something. Run it
with `npm run typecheck`, which uses vue-tsc - a superset of tsc that also
checks SFC templates against their script blocks.
WHY typescript 6 AND NOT 7
TypeScript 7.0 (stable July 2026, Go-native, 8-12x faster) ships no stable
programmatic API until 7.1, so typescript-eslint and the Vue/Svelte/Astro
template checkers cannot run on it. With 29 single-file components, losing
vue-tsc is disqualifying. Revisit when 7.1 restores the API; nothing in this
file will need to change.
OPT-IN, NOT WHOLESALE
`checkJs` is false. A file joins the check by putting `// @ts-check` on its
first line - or, for an SFC, on the first line inside `<script setup>`.
Switching it on globally reports 427 errors, most of them in library code
under a parity freeze - not a review anybody can do usefully in one sitting.
THE LEDGER - what is checked, and what the rest would cost
Measured with `npx vue-tsc --noEmit --checkJs`, which ignores the per-file
opt-in and reports the whole surface. Treat these as a ratchet: an area joins
the list above the line, and never leaves it.

STRICTNESS
`strict` is on but `noImplicitAny` is off. That combination is deliberate for
annotated JS: strict null checking is where the real defects are (it is what
found the nullable-controller and the pop()-may-be-undefined cases), while
requiring an explicit type on every parameter of a 2014-era codebase would
bury those under thousands of trivia.
